exercises.instruction:
Read the situations and write sentences with 'd better or 'd better not. Choose a verb from:
check · disturb · go · put · reserve · take

items.prompt: You're going out for a walk with a friend. It looks as if it might rain.
You and Kate plan to go to a restaurant tonight. It will be busy.
answers: We'd better check what time the film starts.

items.prompt: Oliver has just cut himself. It's bleeding and he'll need a plaster on it.
answers: You'd better put a plaster on it.

items.prompt: Rebecca doesn't look well this morning – not well enough to go to work.
answers: You'd better not go to work this morning.

items.prompt: You're going to the cinema, but you're not sure what time the film starts.
answers: I'd better check what time the film starts.
We'd better check what time the film starts.

items.prompt: You need to talk to your boss, but she's very busy right now.
answers: I'd better not disturb her right now.
We'd better not disturb her right now.

exercises.instruction: Is had better OK in these sentences? Change to should where necessary.

items.prompt: I have an appointment in ten minutes. I'd better go now or I'll be late.
You'd better set your alarm. You have to get up early tomorrow.
I'm glad you came to see us. You'd better come more often.
She'll be sad if we don't invite her to the party, so we'd better invite her.
It's nearly time to go out. I'd better get ready.
I think everybody had better learn a foreign language.
answers: Everybody should learn a foreign language.

items.prompt: We've just missed the last bus. We'd better get a taxi.

better not be late. It's an important meeting.

exercises.instruction: Read the situations and write sentences with It's time (somebody did something).

items.prompt: You're at a friend's house. You planned to go home at 11 o'clock. It's already 11 o'clock now. (I / go)
You haven't had a holiday for a very long time. You need one now. (I / holiday)
answers: It's time I had a holiday.

items.prompt: It's 10 o'clock. It's after the children's bedtime. You think they should be in bed. (children / bed)
answers: It's time the children were in bed.
It's time the children went to bed.

items.prompt: You didn't realise it was so late. You need to start cooking dinner. (start / cook)
answers: It's time I started cooking dinner.

items.prompt: Kate is always complaining about everything. You think she complains too much. (stop / complaining)
answers: It's time she stopped complaining about everything.
It's time Kate stopped complaining about everything.

items.prompt: The company you work for has been badly managed for a long time. You think some changes should be made. (changes / make)
answers: It's time some changes were made in the way the company is run.
